findings.defect: Definition 'A numerical quantity that is not a whole number' is wrong: 4/4, 2/1, 12/4 are fractions equal to whole numbers, and the lesson itself writes 4/4=1, 2/1 and 12/4=3. Also contradicts improper fraction 3/2 in s5 under a 'part of a whole' only model.

Conflates the whole (the bag = 1) with a quantity (2 kg): 'The whole bag can be represented by the fraction 2 over 1 (the whole)'. 'Half' is then never shown as the fraction 1/2 of the bag; instead 2/1 / 2 = 2/2 = 1 kg and 'keeps the other kg: 2/2 = 1/1'. Muddles the unit-whole idea that is the core of objective 1.

Labels (3/4)/(1/4) = 3/1 = 3 as an 'Incorrect Answer'. It is mathematically correct and is a legitimate method (same-denominator division: divide numerators, i.e. count how many quarters in three quarters). Branding a valid strategy an error is misleading.
Error 1/4+1/2=1/6 is not the typical misconception (adding numerators and denominators gives 2/6=1/3); no diagnosis of why the error occurs. Correction 3/4 is correct.

Objective 3 'Compare ... fractions' is never taught or practised (no comparison items). Division of fractions (WE1, WE2, error 2, takeaway 'clear methods for ... division') is not an objective and the closing says division comes in the next lesson - internal contradiction. Unlike-denominator work (warm-up 2, GP2, GP3, Tier 3, exit 2) exceeds the stated 'like denominators' objective without teaching the common-denominator method explicitly.

Core content (adding/subtracting like-denominator fractions, unit fractions of 2 kg) is upper-primary level (e.g. CCSS 4.NF.B.3), well below G7; Tier 3 items are no harder than Tier 1. Reading level FK 12.8 is simultaneously too high.
Two items, unkeyed. Item 2 (1/2-1/3) uses unlike denominators, outside objective 2. Neither assesses representation, comparison or simplification.
Hook problems (half-kilogram packets for 2 or 3 kg; LD$150 budget with no price) are never resolved; sharing among neighbours never quantified.
'palm oil represented as two whole fractions' is meaningless text.
Conflates 'the whole' (the referent unit) with 'whole number'.
Palm oil measured in kg and 'bag of palm oil' (sold by liquid volume locally); s3 uses litres - inconsistent units.
Single MOE code (ratios/percentages) is keyword-matched and unverified.
